newsitem.title: JAPAN: Australia asks Japan not to use rice import as aid.
newsitem.headline: Australia asks Japan not to use rice import as aid.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard urged Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto not to use imported rice as food aid to poor countries during talks in Canberra, a transcript of their conversations showed on Wednesday.

The transcript, which was prepared by the Japanese embassy in Canberra and was made known to Reuters after being sent to officials in Tokyo, said Hashimoto shrugged off the request and said donations of foreign rice were in line with World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.
Last November, the Japanese government announced plans to to send nearly 60,000 tonnes of rice to poor countries in Africa, Asia and Central America. It has already started to implement that plan.
Local grain traders say the rice aid is an attempt to reduce swollen rice stocks in Japan. Good harvests over the past two years have boosted stocks in warehouses in Japan.
The transcript said Howard requested Hashimoto to "stop using imported rice as food aid". But Hashimoto replied that "the rice donations were in line with the WTO's rules".

Under an agreement reached in 1993 in the Uruguay Round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), Japan pledged to gradually open up its long-closed rice market and committed itself to importing a specific quantity of rice per year.
Hashimoto was in Canberra on Tuesday for talks with Howard following a meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Friday.
